exercise1.prompt: Convert "10" to an integer, multiply by 5, print the result
exercise1.hint: int("10") turns the text into the number 10. Multiplying the string by 5 instead would repeat it, giving 1010101010.

exercise2.prompt: Print "Hello, Alice! You are 25 years old."

cases.name: prints the full message
cases.expect_stdout: Hello, Alice! You are 25 years old.

hiddenCases.name: age holds the number 25, not the text

exercise2.hint: print() puts a space between comma-separated pieces, so watch where the spaces and punctuation land. Building the sentence with an f-string gives you exact control.

questions.prompt: A user types 12 when asked input("Age: "). Which value does input return?
questions.explain: input always returns text. Convert it with int when a whole-number calculation is required. This distinction prevents accidentally repeating or joining digits as text.
Multiplying a string by an integer repeats it. This is the classic bug from forgetting to convert input().
int() raises ValueError when the text does not describe a number, which is a good thing: it fails loudly.

questions.prompt: How do you combine a name and an age in one message?
questions.explain: The f-string works with any types. Concatenating with + fails if age is a number, because you cannot add an int to a str.

questions.prompt: Match each idea to its meaning.
right: Converts whole-number text to an integer
Converts decimal text to a floating-point number
Returns text supplied by the user
questions.hint: Think about the type before and after conversion. input itself does not convert digits into numbers.
questions.explain: input("Age: "): Returns text supplied by the user. int("12"): Converts whole-number text to an integer. float("2.5"): Converts decimal text to a floating-point number.

questions.prompt: Arrange these steps in the intended order.
questions.hint: Find the first step that does not depend on any earlier result. Then follow each dependency.
questions.explain: Conversion must happen before addition; otherwise Python is asked to add a string and an integer.

questions.label: Predict the first line of output (without surrounding quotes).
questions.prompt:
raw = "12"
quantity = int(raw)
print(raw * 2)
print(quantity * 2)

First output line: ___
questions.hint: Trace each line in order and write down the current values. Stop at the first print call.
questions.explain: The first multiplication repeats a string twice. After int converts the text, multiplication performs arithmetic. The same operator behaves differently because its operands have different types.
